record.original_question: Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower limit of (f(n) - n)/√n satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) - n)/√n ≤ √3?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.5 (Lai[30]) lim inf n→∞ f(n) − n / √n ≤ √3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $f(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a simple graph on $n$ vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Determine whether
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{f(n)-n}{\sqrt{n}} \le \sqrt{3}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Lai) that liminf (f(n)-n)/√n ≤ √3 remains open. Known results give only lower bounds: Shi (1988) proved ≥ √2, Lai (2017) improved this to √(2+7654/19071), and subsequent works pushed it to √(2+40/99) and √(2+2562/6911). Upper bounds give f(n) ≤ 1.98√n + n (Boros–Caro–Füredi–Yuster), but the conjectured √3 limsup-type upper bound has not been established.

status_evidence.title: A graph without two cycles of the same length (Lai)
status_evidence.snippet: Improved lower bounds liminf (f(n)-n)/√n ≥ √(2 + 40/99), better than √2 (Shi 1988) and √(2 + 7654/19071) (Lai 2017).
status_evidence.claim: Only lower bounds towards the conjecture have been improved; the √3 upper bound remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on cycles — Lai, Liu
status_evidence.claim: The statement is listed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A Lower Bound for the Number of Edges in a Graph Containing No Two Cycles of the Same Length
status_evidence.claim: Active research yields only lower bound progress, not resolution of the √3 conjecture.
